testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A truck may need to weigh less than the legal maximum when driven on:
questions.explanation: Some driving conditions are not safe at full legal weight. Be careful when driving in bad weather or on mountain roads.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: A warm, stuffy cab makes you sleepy. Open a window, use a vent, or turn on air conditioning to keep the cab cool and stay alert.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, the air compressor:

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Sends air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls how it works.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:
questions.explanation: A poorly balanced load makes the vehicle harder and more dangerous to control.

questions.question: All air tanks must have:
questions.explanation: Air tanks must have drain valves. Use them to remove oil and water that build up in the tanks. These valves can be operated by hand or automatically.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within the road you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within the road you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive so you can stop your vehicle completely within the distance you can see ahead on the road.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery when rain first starts falling?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain starts, water mixes with oil and grease on the road surface, creating a slippery film. As rain continues, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: Before going downhill, you should shift to a lower gear:

options.text: As you speed up going downhill.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Downshift before going downhill. Shifting into a lower gear at high speed can damage your transmission and stop engine braking. Choose a safe speed based on hill steepness, length, vehicle weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: If your load is found to be too long during inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure flags and lights for the oversized load are secured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure flags and lights for the oversized load are secured.
questions.explanation: If your load is oversized, make sure all required signs, flags, lights, and reflectors are properly fastened. Check that you have all required permits.

questions.question: You should shift to a higher gear based on:

options.text: Oil pressure and air brake pressure.

questions.explanation: Shift up based on two things: engine speed (rpm) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle manual for the correct rpm range, and watch your speedometer to know when to shift up.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in how long?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: In cold weather, how often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: If a vehicle is tailgating you, let it pass. This gives you more space in front of your vehicle so you can avoid sudden braking. Speeding up is dangerous because the other driver may tailgate you at an even higher speed.

questions.question: What can happen if your vehicle has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It may get better fuel mileage
It may be hard to see the road
The tires may not hold the weight

questions.explanation: A high center of gravity increases the risk of your vehicle tipping over. This happens when cargo is piled high or heavy items are on top of the load.

questions.question: Which item is NOT acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes spare fuses; three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares; and a fire extinguisher that is charged and rated properly.

questions.question: What problem can a flapping cargo cover cause while driving?

options.text: It lets air cool the cargo

questions.explanation: A cargo cover should not flap while driving. It can tear loose, exposing the cargo and blocking your view or the view of other drivers.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should the coolant temperature gauge do?

options.text: Slowly rise to normal operating temperature
Jump quickly to normal operating temperature
Flash until it reaches normal operating temperature

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly rise to normal operating temperature
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature gauge should gradually rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, how far ahead can you see?
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. When driving at night, adjust your speed so you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat with a loud bang, when does the truck feel the effect?

options.text: Only if the flat tire is near the front
Only if the truck is carrying a load

questions.explanation: There is usually a short delay between hearing a tire fail and feeling the truck respond. This delay can make a driver think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: If you operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, which license should you get?
questions.explanation: To operate in both excepted and non-excepted intrastate commerce, you must get a non-excepted intrastate commerce license.

questions.question: When inspecting a power steering-equipped vehicle, you should check that:

options.text: The fluid is at the correct level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the correct level.
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level on power steering systems. Look for leaks and repair them before driving.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, what is the maximum air leakage rate during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: Double combination vehicles must not lose more than 4 psi of air per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Is usually aware of their surroundings.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower perception, delayed decision-making, and poor actions. Avoid distracted drivers when possible.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to do which of the following?
questions.explanation: The test may include straight line backing, offset back parking on the right or left, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs on a vehicle that show what hazardous cargo is being carried.
A type of tire for snowy roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs on a vehicle that show what hazardous cargo is being carried.
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the type of hazard in the cargo.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat makes the load unstable. The truck may become top-heavy and the swinging meat can affect steering. Use extra caution on curves and ramps when carrying such loads.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has one air brake system with two sets of controls.
Has one air brake system for each side of the truck.
Has two brakes for each wheel.
Has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of brakes.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems that work with one brake control. One system usually brakes the rear axle. The other brakes the front axle.

questions.question: Why should you do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order every time?

options.text: You will not forget any steps.
The form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will not forget any steps.
questions.explanation: Using the same routine every time helps you learn the steps and remember to check everything.

questions.question: A maximum safe speed sign means:

options.text: It is a suggestion. Vehicles may travel faster than posted.
It only applies to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.
It only applies to passenger cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: In hot weather, how can you prevent your tires and engine from overheating?
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the hotter your engine and tires become. In very hot weather, reducing your speed helps prevent overheating.

questions.question: What happens when driving in extremely hot weather?

options.text: You need to remove oil from the engine.
It is safer with less coolant.

questions.explanation: Hot weather causes air inside tires to expand and increase pressure. This can be dangerous. Keep enough oil and coolant in your engine to prevent overheating.

questions.question: What happens to your CDL if you are convicted of an alcohol-related offense in your personal vehicle?

options.text: Your CDL is only affected if you refused a breath test.
You lose your CDL for one year.
A sticker is placed on your CDL.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose your CDL for one year.
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is suspended, canceled, or revoked for an alcohol-related offense, a controlled substance offense, or a felony, you will lose your CDL for one year.

questions.question: What is a good rule to follow when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to signal other drivers.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know what you plan to do. Keep your signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: How can you increase visibility when other vehicles have trouble seeing you at dawn or dusk?
questions.explanation: At dawn or dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: How should you stop a vehicle that uses air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop an air brake vehicle, push the brake pedal down. The harder you press, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign that a person is drowsy?
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving is dangerous. Warning signs include frequent blinking, eyes closing on their own, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes. Feeling hungry is not a sign of drowsiness.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand so you can eat and drink.
With one hand at a time, alternating hands.
By cracking it for a better grip.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands for proper control. Place your hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems use alcohol?

options.text: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
To make the compressor run more efficiently.
To lubricate parts of the braking system.
To prevent rust from forming on air brake valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in air brake valves.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the braking system to stop ice from forming.

questions.question: During the driving skills test, what may your examiner ask you to recall after passing under an overpass?

options.text: If there was a shoulder near the roadway.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, your examiner may ask you to recall the posted clearance or height of an overpass you drove under.

questions.question: What should you do if you are driving while drowsy?

options.text: Keep driving and finish your trip.

questions.explanation: The only way to deal with drowsiness while driving is to stop and sleep. Caffeine and other drugs may help you stay awake temporarily, but you will become even more tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: In areas where water pools on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water pools on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water collects on the road. Low tire pressure or worn tire tread makes it more likely. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What do air tank drains do?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tank.
Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and compressor oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have tanks that collect water and compressor oil. These must be drained to prevent damage. Use manual drains at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain the tanks in an air brake system?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil. If water builds up in the system and freezes in cold weather, it can cause brake failure.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually located?
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve is located in the first air tank that receives air from the compressor.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the maximum air leak during a static leakage test is ____ in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test for a single vehicle with air brakes, the leak rate must be no more than 2 psi in one minute. If the leak is faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the maximum air leak during a static leakage test is:
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test for a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the leak rate must be no more than 3 psi in one minute. If the leak is faster, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Which of the following can prevent someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers them a security threat.
They are a lawful U.S. citizen.
They work for a foreign company.
They do not have perfect vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) considers them a security threat.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you renounce your U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent U.S. resident, are wanted for or convicted of certain serious crimes, are judged mentally defective or committed to a mental institution, or are deemed a security threat by the TSA.

questions.question: When alley docking, how should your vehicle be parked?

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
At an angle within the boundaries of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the boundaries of the parking space.
questions.explanation: To alley dock, pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle into the alley. Park it straight within the boundaries of the parking space.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They help drivers see a wider area.
They are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Curved convex mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: What is true about pre-trip vehicle inspections?

options.text: They are not required if you use the vehicle regularly.
They are not required for trips under 100 miles.
Only a mechanic can perform them.

questions.explanation: State and federal law requires drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving.
